Think deeply and do the research before you answer. Do not reason from memory about this
repository — read the code, run the query, and quote what it actually said.

Ground every claim in something you ran:

- Prefer the repo's own instruments over a hand-rolled re-derivation. If a function already
  answers the question, call it rather than reimplementing its rule.
- A zero is not a measurement until a positive control proves the query could see its
  corpus. Run the control in the same corpus, with the same tool and the same flags.
- When a result surprises you, re-run it somewhere else before believing it. An
  environmental defect reproduces exactly, so two readings taken the same way are one
  measurement performed twice.
- Name the query, never only its answer. A count that is not reproducible is a claim about
  the past.

Say plainly what you measured, what you could not measure, and which parts of the answer
rest on inference rather than evidence.

Rules this invokes (CLAUDE.md):

- Investigation discipline
- Ledger and evidence discipline
